note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 54; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 13) on data/benches/titration_curve.json: a titration's curve. The pH against the base run in rises slowly, then leaps at the end point; its steepest point is the end point, and the acid's concentration follows.
title: Experiment: a titration's curve

steps.title: Fill the burette
steps.text: Pick up the sodium hydroxide, right-click the burette, type 55 and click "pour".

steps.title: 25 mL of the unknown acid
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click the acid: it draws to its mark.

steps.title: Into the flask
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click the flask.

steps.title: Until it is empty
steps.text: Wait until the pipette has run out.

steps.title: The burette over the flask
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click a free square; then pick up the burette and click the flask.

steps.title: Log the pH
steps.text: Right-click the flask, click "+ pH" under its readings to write it down, then open the notebook and click "1 s": it logs the pH every second.
steps.why: A logger writes a reading down at every whole second: the notebook's rows are moments, and what two loggers of one interval write share them.

steps.title: Log the burette
steps.text: Close the notebook, right-click the burette, click "+ mL", open the notebook again and click "1 s".

steps.title: A slow stream
steps.text: Close the notebook, right-click the burette, drag its tap to about 15 % and click 60x.
steps.why: Slowly enough that the logger catches the leap near the end point in a dozen points.

steps.title: Shut it
steps.text: Drag the burette's tap shut. Open the notebook: x the burette's reading, y the pH. The end point is where the curve is steepest.
steps.why: Halfway up the leap the acid and the base are equal: H2SO4 + 2 NaOH. Its volume of the 0.100 M base holds twice the acid's moles.

report.label: the end point
report.why: The truth is the base that held twice the acid's moles. Read from the plot, where the pH leaps (the middle of the leap); a burette reads within 0.05 mL, a logger every second.

report.label: the acid's concentration
report.why: c = 0.100 x V(end point) / (2 x 25.00 mL). The base's label is 0.100 M; it is 0.0997 (0.040 mol in 401 mL), and the pipette delivers its own 25 mL within 0.03.
